title: Broker audit trail and attribution backfill
position: Each pattern should be tracked as a Provenance rule: BROKER-AUDIT-001 through BROKER-AUDIT-003
rationale: Audit trail requires structured tracing with project_id in every handler span, identity attribution on all mutations (user/agent/service/api_key), and content-addressed deduplication for contract versions.
context: Codebase scan identified 3 enforcement patterns in broker for audit trail

title: Broker authentication pipeline enforcement backfill
position: Each pattern should be tracked as a Provenance rule: BROKER-AUTH-001 through BROKER-AUTH-006
rationale: Authentication is the first layer of defense. These rules enforce Bearer-only extraction, token type discrimination, RS256 JWT validation, control plane delegation, hashed cache keys, and JWKS refresh rate limiting.
context: Codebase scan identified 6 enforcement patterns in broker for authentication

title: Broker authorization and permission model backfill
position: Each pattern should be tracked as a Provenance rule: BROKER-AUTHZ-001 through BROKER-AUTHZ-006
rationale:
Authorization model gates every handler with type-safe permission extractors (RequirePermission

), hierarchical scopes (admin>write>read), mandatory auth extraction, proposal state machine enforcement, JWT permission merging, and 32 fine-grained permission slugs.
context: Codebase scan identified 6 enforcement patterns in broker for authorization

title: Broker information leakage prevention backfill
position: Each pattern should be tracked as a Provenance rule: BROKER-LEAK-001 through BROKER-LEAK-003
rationale: Information leakage prevention uses 404-not-403 for cross-project access (anti-enumeration), token prefix-only logging, and generic RFC 7807 error titles to prevent information disclosure.
context: Codebase scan identified 3 enforcement patterns in broker for leakage prevention

title: Broker infrastructure security backfill
position: Each pattern should be tracked as a Provenance rule: BROKER-INFRA-001 through BROKER-INFRA-004
rationale: Infrastructure security enforces request timeouts (30s), fail-closed on control plane unavailability, PostgreSQL-only database protocol, and parameterized SQL queries across all 21 repository files.
context: Codebase scan identified 4 enforcement patterns in broker for infrastructure security

title: Broker input validation and safety backfill
position: Each pattern should be tracked as a Provenance rule: BROKER-INPUT-001 through BROKER-INPUT-003
rationale: Input validation prevents malformed data and resource exhaustion. Progressive transaction validation, pagination limit caps, and startup config validation protect the system boundary.
context: Codebase scan identified 3 enforcement patterns in broker for input validation

title: Broker multi-tenant isolation backfill
position: Each pattern should be tracked as a Provenance rule: BROKER-TENANT-001 through BROKER-TENANT-005
rationale: Tenant isolation is enforced at three layers (handler, service, SQL) with defense-in-depth. These rules cover project-scoped queries, project allowlist, explicit ownership verification, cross-org prevention, and body/auth consistency checks.
context: Codebase scan identified 5 enforcement patterns in broker for tenant isolation

title: Pin an absent Rust SDK to the CLI release
position: When the selected Cargo package has no provenance-sdk declaration, Cargo init adds provenance-sdk with an exact requirement equal to the provenance-cli version.
rationale: The CLI and SDK ship as one release and must begin compatible. An exact initial requirement prevents an unreviewed later SDK release from changing behavior, while existing compatible registry and explicit development declarations remain untouched.

title: Restore only Cargo add owned changes
position: Coordinate Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock as one guarded pair: restore both pre-command states only while both match the observed post-Cargo state, refuse both after a concurrent edit or first replacement failure, and compensate the first file if the second replacement fails.
rationale: A broad repository rollback duplicates state ownership. Unconditional Cargo restoration can overwrite concurrent edits, while an uncoordinated pair can strand one pre-command file beside one post-Cargo file. Pair comparison, ordered replacement, and compensation limit cleanup to demonstrably owned changes and report when the pair cannot safely move together.

inputs.summary: Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock alone need explicit guarded pair rollback after cargo add, including refusal and replacement-failure behavior.

title: Convex chosen as backend over custom WebSocket infrastructure
position: Use Convex as the backend for Provenance
rationale: Convex provides reactive queries, server-side functions, real-time sync, and document-based storage without building custom WebSocket infrastructure. First-party WorkOS integration simplifies auth. Trade-off: 1MB document size limit requires normalized schema with separate tables instead of embedded sub-documents.
context: Provenance requires real-time collaborative editing where multiple users see changes instantly. Options considered: custom WebSocket server, Firebase/Supabase, Convex.

title: Immutable dispositions are the sole state authority
position: Model proposal, assertion, and disposition as three immutable record kinds and derive effective state from them; do not persist a mutable promotion-state authority
rationale: The mutable promotion_state column lost on four counts from the blocking review: caller-selected rather than verified; proposal mutation and decision append are separate shard writes that can diverge; builds_on lineage pointed at state that could flip under descendants; six ingress paths enforced different contracts. A global batch-disposal queue lost on the evidence that batch disposal never happened.

title: One Markdown reading governs checking and serving
position: Use the published page map as target authority and parse links with the server's Markdown options
rationale: The separate plain-parser check lost because it treated a footnote definition as a broken reference link while the extended serving parser rendered it as a footnote.

title: Domain placement follows the refinement graph
position: Attribute each requirement to its direct and inherited domains and each rule through its producing requirements
rationale: Direct-domain-only attribution lost because an unclassified child and its rules disappeared from the authored domain of their classified ancestor.

title: Evidence site states are report findings
position: Record the enclosing symbol and content identity beside each evidence site's file and line coordinate. A later scan resolves that anchor before classifying the site, and the classifications stay derived report findings
rationale: A line number moves with unrelated edits, so the coordinate alone cannot re-identify a site. Storing the classification would turn a derived finding into canonical graph state the next scan would have to repair

inputs.summary: Glossary entries for evidence site, evidence anchor, and evidence path at commit 6ec714d

title: One shared gap computation for every surface
position: Port the wiki assembler's gap taxonomy into a shared compute_gaps in the store, add the contradicts-pair, open-question, and unexplored-topic kinds, and delete the wiki's private gap logic
rationale: Letting the wiki keep its own gap logic lost because wiki and prime were already drifting and already disagreed on orphan detection. Having the shaping skill assemble the frontier from five list commands lost because it is the hand-wiring the design forbids.

title: Graph ids are valid by construction
position: Keep the id character decision in one predicate called by private constructors and handwritten deserializers
rationale: Duplicated constructor predicates lost because they could drift, and derived deserialization lost because it bypassed constructor validation for stored JSON.

title: Graph references use full verified identity
position: Resolve revision text at issuance, store a full lowercase commit, and rederive repository, graph, and reference identities on every read
rationale: Persisting a branch, tag, or abbreviation lost because it can move or become ambiguous; trusting recorded identity fields lost because the graph can be presented from another repository or with changed content.

title: A human canonical artifact ratifies acceptance
position: A human-authored accepted disposition naming an existing canonical artifact stands without a prior assertion
rationale: Requiring every acceptance to follow a swarm assertion lost because a tournament winner is ratified by the human action that creates the canonical artifact, and the extra assertion made that flow impossible.

title: Typed implementation bindings retire in place
position: Removing an implementedBy declaration marks the owned canonical binding retired. Declaring the relationship again clears retirement on the same binding id. Reconciliation stays inside the rules the same spec owns
rationale: Deleting the binding would lose why the rule was once considered implemented. Leaving it active would preserve a claim the spec deliberately removed. An equal declaration owner used by another spec does not broaden the retirement boundary

inputs.summary: Accepted ADR: implementedBy removal retires the owned binding in place

title: Init does the whole onboarding, identically on every channel
position: provenance init installs the bundled skills and injects the instruction block in one run. Behavior is identical whether the CLI came from a release archive, npm, or npx, because npx provenance is the same binary
rationale: A channel-specific onboarding step would make npx and a release install behave differently for no gain. Both the skills installer and init are idempotent, so re-running init stays safe

inputs.summary: Ben: init should install the skills; npx adds nothing distinct

title: Plan initialization before project writes
position: Build and validate one in-memory projection of the manifest, skills, legacy cleanup, AGENTS.md, and .gitignore before writing any project-owned path.
rationale: Chosen over sequential preflight plus writes because a late conflict or invalid planned manifest could otherwise strand earlier changes. Chosen over a repository snapshot transaction because initialization should classify its own finite outputs rather than become a second state engine.

inputs.summary: Use one complete InitPlan, pure projections, planned graph validation, and per-file atomic replacement; do not claim crash-wide multi-file atomicity.

title: Upgrade only hash-owned installed skills
position: Init replaces a prior-version installed skill only when its Provenance stamp hash still matches the current payload; an edited or unstamped file is preserved and init fails.
rationale: Stamp byte equality rejects every release-version change even when the installed payload is untouched. The existing payload hash distinguishes that safe upgrade from user edits; unconditional overwrite would destroy those edits.

title: The injected block is lean and CLI-only
position: Inject the fixed 160-token block ratified 2026-08-24. No ownership markers. The block never names .provenance/state; agents reach the graph only through CLI commands. Changes to Requirements, Rules, and past decisions go through a Proposal that a human decides
rationale: Marker header and footer blocks were rejected as noise. A state-path reference was rejected because agents that open the shards flood their context window. Prohibition wording was rejected because it reads as if the product cannot change; the Proposal path states the same boundary as process. The block replaces the retired managed marker-delimited skills section that legacy cleanup removes

inputs.summary: Design conversation: ratified block text and the rejected alternatives

title: Init injects the block and owns it by heading
position: provenance init injects the instruction block. The installer owns the section under the exact Provenance heading and updates it in place. A renamed heading transfers ownership to the user and the installer then leaves the section alone
rationale: The block is useful in repositories that never install skills, so it belongs to init, not skills install. Heading match gives an update path without the rejected markers. Inject-once was rejected because stale instructions mislead agents

inputs.summary: Ben picked init, heading ownership, and the decides wording

title: Invalid confidence is not repaired
position: Reject invalid graph scores and warn on invalid source annotations while retaining the annotation default
rationale: Silent clamping lost because a repaired endpoint looks authored; aborting the whole scan lost because one malformed source comment should not prevent scanning the repository.

title: Later decisions use the modern lifecycle
position: Keep the retired promotion-decisions shard at the exact shipped-v1 audit and write every later decision as a modern disposition
rationale: Appending modern decisions to the retired shard lost after ac661a2 changed the compiled audit from 76 to 79 rows and bypassed modern actor and assertion authority.

title: Mirror Statesman contract metadata vocabulary in external test annotations
position: Use Allure's label/link primitive architecture but populate it with Statesman's existing vocabulary: name, description, tags from Contract trait; rule, coverage, confidence, notes from RuleContract. No epic/feature/story.
rationale: Consistency: coverage data looks the same whether it comes from a Statesman contract or an annotated external test. The Provenance coverage model doesn't need to distinguish sources -- the fields are identical. No new concepts to learn for teams already using Statesman contracts. Non-technical viewers in Provenance see the same metadata (description, tags, coverage level) regardless of how coverage was established. Avoids positioning Statesman as a PM tool.
context: External test annotations need a vocabulary for describing tests and linking them to rules. Three options considered: (1) invent new annotation-specific fields, (2) adopt Allure's epic/feature/story hierarchy, (3) replicate the fields that Statesman contracts already carry. Allure's label/link primitive model is sound, but Allure's organizational labels (epic/feature/story) are project management concepts that conflict with Statesman's strategic positioning.

title: Resolve nested Rust paths from the package
position: implemented_by! resolves its file literal against CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR before store normalization persists a path relative to the discovered Provenance repository.
rationale: Persisting the raw literal drops a nested workspace member's directory, while persisting the resolved absolute path is machine-specific. Package resolution followed by repository normalization preserves both file identity and portability.

title: Only default generated output updates gitignore
position: Append .provenance/wiki/ only when the caller omits --out
rationale: Automatic gitignore mutation for caller-selected output paths lost because explicit paths are caller-owned rather than a repository-generated default.

title: Pinned graphs project asserted scope only
position: Project only canonical families of the selected scope, stripping collaboration fields on export and refusing excluded or foreign-scope records on import
rationale: Exporting the repository wholesale lost because discussion and unfinished ideation are not graph assertions; foreign-scope records lost because one scope's digest and counts would describe mixed ownership.

title: Posting reconciles active threads
position: Select the oldest active thread by created_at and id, then archive every other active sibling in the posting write
rationale: Refusing the post lost to the reconcile option in imported PROV-IDEATE-032; the shipped path accepts the post and repairs duplicate active siblings under the publication lock.

title: Add proof as a sixth verification method
position: Extend the verification methods with proof: a machine-checked proof outside the test runner backs the rule, and the marked site is the bridge that pins the implementation to the proved model.
rationale: The cmdcache adoption experiment tried several formal-verification strategies and settled on Lean 4: a hand model with total injectivity proofs, an Aeneas extraction spike, and a golden-vector conformance test binding the Rust implementation to the model. Conformance understates that evidence; the word proof carries the claim. The proof checker runs in the adopter's CI; the scan reads the claim, consistent with how every other method word is trusted.

inputs.summary: The Lean 4 model proofs, Aeneas extraction spike, and golden-vector conformance bridge that motivated the sixth method word.

title: Proposals are consulted on demand
position: Consult undisposed proposals only through exact evidence-path or typed-territory demand and exclude them from Prime and global batch review
rationale: A global review inbox lost because 153 backtrace proposals accumulated without batch disposal while the only reviewed section was disposed when work demanded it; inferred matching also lost because it widens territory beyond recorded evidence.

title: Recovery trusts resolved cache children
position: Resolve each transaction directory to a real direct cache child and operate only on that resolved path
rationale: Trusting the marker pathname lost because dot-dot segments and symlinked leaves could steer whole-tree rename or deletion outside the transaction directory.

title: Recursive requirements replace initiative/epic/story hierarchy
position: Use a single Requirement type that recurses to arbitrary depth via parentId
rationale: Requirements compose recursively via bind (refinement produces sub-requirements). The hierarchy IS the recursion -- no separate concepts needed. This follows the monad pattern: each requirement is a unit of work that can be decomposed further. Status flows naturally from leaves to root. Cross-domain sharing works via edges (depends_on, contradicts) between any nodes in the tree.
context: Traditional project management uses distinct container types (initiative, epic, story, task). Provenance needed a way to decompose work at arbitrary depth without artificial tier limits.

title: Resolution inputs are named, not graph-resolved
position: Require nonblank reference and summary text without requiring the reference to resolve to a graph record
rationale: Graph-only references lost because legislation, files, and conversations may stay external; repairing or dropping blanks lost because later text would falsely look like an original decision input.

title: Review required is distinct from stale
position: A restated requirement statement writes one review record per produced rule, naming the field, its value before and after, and when the change landed. A verification run arriving after the change clears that rule's review. Stale stays reserved for evidence whose code changed
rationale: When only a sentence changes, no file moved and no test was touched. Reusing stale would teach readers to distrust the word. The record is the authority: plan reads it rather than inferring, and it reports previewed reviews apart by having no timestamp

inputs.summary: Accepted ADR: requirement restatement raises per-rule review records distinct from stale

title: The function is the rule
position: A rule is a function in the codebase, or a type whose construction is the proof; #[rule(id)] binds it to its graph record, and no primitive, registry, or runtime exists
rationale: Fiat's runtime and define_rule lost: a primitive earns existence only when something must call rules through Provenance, and nothing does. The OpenFisca insight (rules are registered executables) is kept without its engine. A wrapper on already-pure functions adds nothing; the attribute is the whole registration.

title: A rule binds implementation, it is not the implementation
position: A Rule is an independent behavioural obligation. The compiled rule marker binds the primary implementation to the Rule and does not define it. This supersedes res_rule_is_the_function
rationale: A Rule must exist before code and survive rewrites, and Unimplemented must stay an ordinary derived absence. Both fail when the function is the Rule. The compiled-marker binding survives from the earlier position

inputs.summary: Accepted ADR: rules are independent of implementation

title: Rules follow human decisions, not code structure
position: Rule granularity follows the decisions humans made: one function with many branches implementing one decision is one rule, and a decision with no function is a requirement whose rule is unwritten
rationale: Rule-per-branch and rule-per-function both lost: the endpoint table is one decision with nine branches, and minting records for structure inflates the graph with entries no human decided. An active rule record with no function is a promise the scanner reports as broken forever - creating one to make a decision look landed is the anti-pattern the shaping skill must stop teaching.

title: Keep Rust authoring semantics in provenance-core
position: Place pure builders, document-decidable structural checks, address construction, canonical authored assembly, and the TypedSpec input family in the existing provenance-core crate.
rationale: A new engine crate or SDK-owned materializer would duplicate ownership. Provenance-core already owns protocol and domain types, stays dependency-light, and is shared by store and wire consumers.

title: Audit Rust crates before publication
position: Do not publish the Rust crates until the DR10 audit covers public APIs, dependency closure, version coupling, engine identity, and MSRV, and Ben records a separate go decision.
rationale: Publishing too early can freeze accidental APIs or an incomplete dependency chain. Graph promotion is not crate publication.

title: Accept design-stage execution uncertainty
position: Accept that Design review executed no code if V1 through V12 and the two Plan-entry checks discharge the uncertainty before reliance.
rationale: The reviews establish ownership and controls from repository evidence. Tests and Plan-entry checks remain required before implementation claims success.

title: Accept discovery-fallback risk with a fixture
position: Accept the no-repository discovery risk with a fixture for the canonicalized start-directory fallback.
rationale: CO-R7-7 closes the current test gap without changing discovery semantics.

title: Accept the static empty-statement finding
position: Accept the static empty-statement finding if V2 verifies the wire and STE rejection paths during execution.
rationale: Independent code reading found no engine wire rejection, but execution is the final check.

title: Accept error-wording risk with pre-capture
position: Accept relocation-time error-wording risk only if current wire wording is captured before the kernel takes ownership.
rationale: CO-R7-4 and CO-R7-5 separate engine-identical wire text from TypeScript-parity build-time text.

title: Treat goldens as change detectors
position: Accept golden files and corpus fixtures as change detectors rather than complete proofs.
rationale: The fixtures protect named behavior while property, conformance, and existing engine tests cover other dimensions.

title: Accept process-global host limits
position: Accept process-global current-directory, environment, and advisory-lock limits and document them for in-process hosts.
rationale: The first API keeps current engine behavior. Documentation makes the concurrency limit explicit.

title: Accept publication risk behind the audit gate
position: Accept publication-surface uncertainty only behind the DR10 audit and a later human go decision.
rationale: Engine version, dependency closure, MSRV, and public API exposure can change the release decision but cannot bypass G1.

title: Accept the heuristic purity check
position: Accept V12 as a compile-time import check plus deterministic property tests, not a formal proof of purity.
rationale: The checks catch the expected dependency and behavior violations without claiming a machine proof.

title: Accept rejection-precedence risk with a fixture
position: Accept rejection-precedence risk only if a multi-defect fixture pins the current per-item first error.
rationale: Static call placement alone does not prove intra-list precedence. CO-R7-3 makes the stronger commitment observable.

title: Accept stranded verification-run risk
position: Accept that aborts, process death, or direct engine use can leave a verification run marked running.
rationale: The facade records ordinary errors and unwinds before propagation. It cannot recover after process termination or bypass by direct consumers.

title: Accept temporary TypeScript mirror risk
position: Accept temporary TypeScript mirror drift while the kernel is authoritative and the cross-SDK corpus monitors parity.
rationale: Deleting TypeScript mirrors is a separate change. V3 detects drift during the redundancy period.

title: A same-owner duplicate rule takes the wire error
position: At build(), a repeated rule declaration merges only when it adds a new owner; a same-owner repeat stays a separate declaration and the shared wire checker rejects it.
rationale: Merge-by-content lost: it let build() accept a document whose wire form the engine refuses, which breaks kernel and wire acceptance identity (PR #150 review round one). A build-only duplicate error lost because it would mint a second wording for a defect the wire checker already names.

title: SDK adapters resolve the repository first
position: Every sdk CLI adapter resolves the repository before it reads stdin or parses the scope.
rationale: Resolution inside the store operations lost: it reordered invocation-level errors, so a bad --repo surfaced only after stdin reached end of file (PR #150 review round two). Resolving first restores the pre-relocation error order and costs one extra canonicalization.

title: Use a thin provenance-sdk facade
position: Add provenance-sdk as re-exports plus verification orchestration, macro projections, settings, a parity ledger, and engine_info().
rationale: These are Rust frontend concerns that do not belong in the pure core. Keeping materialization, validation, identity, planning, and mutation outside the facade prevents a second semantic layer.

title: Use Cargo compatibility for the Rust SDK
position: Use Cargo semver for in-process compatibility and Cargo path or patch configuration for explicit development overrides.
rationale: An in-process Rust consumer resolves crates through Cargo and does not need a duplicate runtime protocol handshake. Wire consumers keep the existing protocol check.

title: Keep the stateful Rust seam in provenance-store
position: Keep identity, reconciliation, ownership refusal, STE write gates, locking, planning, and mutation in provenance-store, and expose its SDK operations as in-process functions.
rationale: The store already owns persistent state and one plan/apply path. A separate provenance-engine crate or CLI library seam would add another owner or lose store behavior.

title: Resolve Rust implementation symbols in provenance-store
position: Resolve implementation symbols to repository files in provenance-store and reject missing or ambiguous matches before apply writes state.
rationale: The scanner supplies evidence, but the stateful apply boundary must own the decision and its no-write refusal behavior.

title: Deliver synchronous Rust verification first
position: Ship synchronous Rust verification first, record callback failure before propagation, and defer asynchronous verification.
rationale: The synchronous API matches current engine operations and TypeScript failure semantics. Async support can follow without delaying the first native Rust surface.

title: verify() anchors the call site inside the repository
position: verify() resolves the compiler's call-site path at the nearest working-directory ancestor that places the file inside the discovered repository; an unresolved path passes through unchanged as a repository-relative claim.
rationale: The raw compile-time path lost: it is workspace-relative, so a crate nested below the repository root records a binding file that does not exist (PR #150 review round one). A CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR capture lost because it forces a macro call form onto every verification site.

title: Preserve typed-spec wire semantics
position: Route wire ingestion through the kernel at the existing pipeline points without changing protocol 4, schema 1, acceptance, first-error order, error wording, or decoded response order.
rationale: Existing TypeScript documents and other wire consumers must keep the same engine contract while semantic code moves to its shared home.

title: The SDK package supplies the engine
position: Each language SDK resolves and runs an engine shipped as a package-manager artifact for the host, discovers the project from the nearest Provenance or Git root when unconfigured, and rejects engines outside its supported protocol range
rationale: An install-script binary download adds a second distribution channel to secure and version. The package manager already delivers a per-host artifact with the SDK, so compatibility is decided by the protocol handshake, not by install-time trust

inputs.summary: POC outcome: façade plus one-shot child-process protocol; engine supplied by the package

title: Simple key-value comment syntax, migrate to native annotations later if needed
position: Use simple @statesman key: value syntax. If native annotations are needed later, a statesman migrate command handles the mechanical transformation.
rationale: Comments should look like comments. The migration from one text format to another is trivial -- a sed one-liner or a CLI migrate command. Don't optimize the comment format for a future that may not come. The simple format is easier to type, easier to read, and easier to parse. Native annotations are a separate concern with their own syntax per language.
context: The annotation format lives in comments. Two syntax options: (1) function-call style like @statesman.rule("CODE") which mirrors what native decorators would look like, or (2) simple key-value like @statesman rule: CODE which is honest about being metadata in a comment. Function-call style has the advantage of being forward-compatible with native annotations but adds visual noise (parens, quotes) to something that is not code.

title: Foreign install targets require force
position: Classify targets by installer ownership and require force only before replacing foreign content
rationale: Treating every symlink as replaceable lost after a0d5c31 removed foreign symlinks; f48d264 retained force-free replacement only for the installer's own canonical symlink.

title: A source pin locates without full identity
position: Accept 7-64 mixed-case hexadecimal source pins while keeping graph-reference commits full and lowercase
rationale: Applying graph-reference identity shape to source pins lost because source pins are reader locators commonly copied in short or uppercase form; applying the looser shape to graph references lost because abbreviations can become ambiguous.

title: Sharded JSONL in git with a stable-id merge driver
position: Keep canonical state as sharded JSONL in git with SQLite as a rebuildable cache, and supply a custom git merge driver that merges by stable record id
rationale: SQLite-as-canonical lost because git cannot merge an opaque binary. Dolt lost because it needs its own storage layer and sync path and still cannot resolve same-field conflicts. One JSON file per record lost on volume at Statesman/SCHADS rule counts. Raw git line merge lost because one record is one line, the wrong merge granularity.

title: Static analysis first, runtime reporters later
position: Start with static analysis. Design the annotation format and Provenance API to support runtime evidence later, but ship the scanner first.
rationale: Static analysis delivers the core value (traceability link from rule to test) with a single tool vs N framework integrations. It establishes the annotation convention that runtime reporters will reuse. The link itself is valuable even without pass/fail -- when a regulation changes, knowing which tests cover the affected rule is immediately actionable. Runtime reporters add richer signal but require per-framework maintenance (Jest, pytest, JUnit, Go) and higher adoption friction. Build the foundation first, enrich later.
context: External test coverage linking needs a delivery strategy. Two approaches: (1) static analysis scanner that extracts annotations from source code without running tests, or (2) runtime test reporters (per-framework plugins) that capture pass/fail results. Both use the same annotation format.

title: Keep automatic download for agent onboarding
position: Interactive onboarding uses the official request form. Agent onboarding downloads automatically when no reusable import exists. Later commands use local data.
rationale: Form-first remains appropriate for people. Form-first for agents lost because limited agents can stop at the form. One onboarding download is cached and reused.

title: Acquire STE dictionary data without redistribution
position: Interactive onboarding uses the official request form. Agent onboarding downloads the official PDF. Each project reuses its imported dictionary.
rationale: This approach supports dictionary checks without publishing ASD data. It avoids repeated downloads and does not depend on a machine-readable release from STEMG.

title: Use ASD-STE100 as the rule authority
position: The checker applies ASD-STE100 directly. Provenance does not define a substitute language.
rationale: A Provenance-owned ruleset lost because it would rename or reinterpret an existing standard and make its syntax findings nonstandard. Custom extensions do not affect the first implementation.

title: Tests verify; only live code enforces
position: Enforcement means the function stands on the live path so a violating state cannot occur; tests verify rules through a closed method vocabulary - exhaustion, property, examples, conformance, construction - and exhaustion over a finite domain is formal proof
rationale: The binding-ladder model (tests as the weakest rung of enforcement) lost because it collapsed two relations into one word: a test stops nothing at runtime. Prover engines lost because checking every case of a finite domain is already a proof and adds a toolchain for nothing.

title: Typed declarations retire in place
position: A typed spec is a complete desired-state document only for records carrying its owner and address prefix. An omitted declaration is marked retired, keeps its stable id and history, and reactivates when declared again
rationale: Omission is too weak a signal for deletion or ownership transfer, so both remain separate operations. Overloading a domain status would mix lifecycle with meaning

inputs.summary: Accepted ADR: omitted typed declarations retire in place

title: TypeScript constructs, Rust reconciles
position: TypeScript owns pure declaration construction with immutable handles. The Rust engine assigns ids, validates and reconciles records, and materializes one canonical rule for a declaration shared across requirements
rationale: Keeping construction pure means importing a declaration module changes nothing until an explicit apply. Letting the host language mutate canonical state would duplicate the engine's identity rules in every SDK

inputs.summary: POC identity rules: immutable handles, static implementation references, shared-rule materialization

title: Disclose missing decisions and rules in the badge
position: Render Resolved (no decisions or rules) without changing persisted requirement status
rationale: Adding an archived status lost for this fix because it would change persisted state, and the first label Resolved (unbacked) lost because review rejected unexplained vocabulary.

title: Plain text wins over speculative reference links
position: Emit an anchor only for an existing web URL or a code path a recognized remote turns into a valid blob URL
rationale: Repository-relative anchors without a known remote lost because they resolve against wiki routes and return 404; treating every bare dotted token as a path lost because prose tokens are indistinguishable.

title: Unsupported layouts fail before conversion
position: Compare raw stored versions with the supported constant before deserialization or shard mutation
rationale: Letting Serde half-read a future layout lost because unknown fields silently disappear; leaving read-modify-write unguarded lost after review showed an unrelated create could launder a version-2 row into version 1.

title: Unverified is absence, derived
position: A rule with no verifies site anywhere is unverified; the state is derived by coverage scan and never stored
rationale: Stored assurance lost: a persisted verified flag is the one copy that can drift, and the annotation-era self-asserted confidence field is the proof of what happens to self-reported metadata. Absence cannot go stale and cannot be forgotten.

title: Verification bindings are canonical relationships
position: Store a first-class verification binding whose stable identity is the verification owner, the canonical rule, and an explicit owner-local key. Method, repository path, and symbol are updateable facts on the same binding. A run is volatile evidence that cites the binding and snapshots its execution context
rationale: File names, line numbers, and callback names change too easily to carry identity. No stored verified status: coverage derives unverified from the absence of both scanner-discovered sites and active canonical bindings. No Test node enters the generic ontology, because that would commit every language integration to a Test lifecycle the POC does not need

inputs.summary: Accepted ADR: binding identity is owner, rule, and owner-local key; runs are volatile evidence

title: Typed verification bindings retire in place
position: A run is desired state only for the owner, file, and key it reports. Reporting a key in a file against a different rule retires the binding that key previously named. Absence from a run retires nothing
rationale: One execution sees only the call sites it happened to run, so a filtered or sharded run must not mass-retire relationships it did not observe, and no run can retire another owner's work. Bindings whose recorded file no longer exists go to the stale gate instead, because a run that never executed the file cannot vouch for it

inputs.summary: Accepted ADR: a run retires only the owner, file, and key it reports; absence retires nothing

title: Verification strength is a per-repo dial
position: How hard a repository verifies is its own call: an examples mark on an existing test is a legitimate first rung that moves a rule out of the unverified list honestly, and proofs are the ceiling for decisions where being wrong destroys something
rationale: A universal proof bar lost on adoption grounds: if every rule demands an exhaustion proof with an independent oracle, people write zero rules. The backfill of this repo is the ceiling demonstration, deliberately not the norm; the on-ramp is one rule in a PR that touches that code anyway.

title: Warn on markers citing retired rules
position: When --validate-rules is requested, coverage scan warns for every marker citing a deprecated or archived rule, and --strict treats that warning like every other scan warning.
rationale: A retired rule no longer establishes current coverage, so silently accepting its markers creates false confidence. The warning names the rule id and its stored status, so a reader can tell it apart from a marker citing an id no rule carries.

title: Stable-id chips distinguish colliding titles
position: Render the shortest distinguishing stable-id suffix and add record kind only when equal ids occur across kinds
rationale: A distinguishing prose clause lost when provenance-c9m.7 selected one short stable-id chip implemented once in the central list renderer; history records no further comparative rationale.

title: Search-first wiki homepage with domain and traceability grafts
position: Make query-first retrieval the homepage's primary action; place a capped authored-domain map immediately after it; finish with one exact traceability finding count linked to dedicated detail.
rationale: Search Launchpad won because it gives known-item retrieval the clearest first action and compresses well on mobile. Domain Atlas lost ownership of the page because taxonomy quality varies, but its authored-domain cards were grafted as the main browse path. Traceability Ledger lost ownership because a full metric sheet would frame reader documentation as a maintenance dashboard, but its exact-count assurance signal and findings link were grafted below domains.
context: Human ratified the hierarchy after reviewing desktop and mobile prototypes: search first, domains second, compact traceability call to action last.
enforcement: Homepage renderer order, scale-contract tests, responsive browser checks, and exact health-detail routing.

title: Wiki publication refuses ambiguous filesystem state
position: Publish through a complete sibling stage, reject unsafe routes and unowned outputs, and leave crash residue for operator action
rationale: Live-tree mutation lost because failure could leave a partial generation; journal syntax as ownership proof lost because it could authorize deletion of caller content; route normalization lost because it silently changed empty segments.

title: Workflowd runs the typed product loop
position: Workflowd adopts the typed spec as the ordinary change path: the spec models obligations chosen from product intent, planning a changed obligation explains its impact, and the agent updates traceability in the same change
rationale: A separate manual repair step after each change is the failure the loop exists to remove. One declaration per implementation detail would turn the spec into an inventory nobody reviews
